sections.text: An enum is a type that can be one of a fixed set of variants. Use it when a value can only be one of a few things.

Variants can carry data, and each variant can carry different data. To do something different for each variant, use match. You'll learn match properly in the last lesson of this unit. For now, read each arm as "if it's this variant, run this code", and notice how the arm pulls the data out of the variant:
Enums can have methods too, in an impl block just like structs:
An enum is like a multiple-choice answer: the value is exactly one of the listed options, never something else.

Rust enums are tagged unions (sum types): unlike C enums or Java's singleton enum constants, each variant can carry its own data, much like a Java sealed interface with record implementations. Together with structs they let you make invalid states unrepresentable.

exercise.prompt:
Add a fourth variant, Mythic, to Rarity, and add Rarity::Mythic to the end of the list so it gets printed too. It should print: Common
Rare
Epic
Mythic
hints: Two places list the rarities: the enum itself and the array in main. Both need the new one.
Add a line Mythic, to the enum. Then add Rarity::Mythic at the end of the array inside the square brackets.

How do you write the East variant of Direction?
